newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SCHARPING PLAYS DOWN KOHL'S RECORD TERM IN OFFICE.
newsitem.headline: SCHARPING PLAYS DOWN KOHL'S RECORD TERM IN OFFICE.

text.p: German opposition Social Democrat parliamentary leader Rudolf Scharping said on Friday Chancellor Helmut Kohl's record term in office was not in itself an achievement.
Kohl, who has been at the helm of Germany's federal government for 14 years, will pass Konrad Adenauer as the longest-serving chancellor this century on October 30.
"It is a remarkable length of time," Scharping, the SPD's failed challenger to Kohl in the 1994 election, told reporters. "But I don't regard it as having merit in itself."

Scharping, who is in Hungary to attend a weekend gathering of European Socialist Party leaders, said he respected Kohl's political achievements, notably German unification and his commitment to Europe, but warned observers not to dwell only on Kohl's accomplishments.
"Kohl is also setting records at home for unemployment, indebtedness and tax burdens," he said.

In a poll published on Friday Germans said they believed Chancellor Helmut Kohl is more interested in European affairs than domestic issues and that his efforts to unite Europe will be his primary mark in history, an opinion poll published on Friday found.
Seventy-nine percent of Germans surveyed by the Emnid institute for the television network N-TV said his main achievement had been in pushing for European integration.
A slightly smaller number, 74 percent, said Kohl's effort to unite East and West Germany in 1990 would go down in history as his main success.
